'''Willie Trill Cauley-Stein''' (born '''Willie Durmond Cauley Jr.'''; August 18, 1993) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] with the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky Wildcats]].

==Early life==
He was born and raised in [[Spearville, Kansas]], population 791.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://www.sactownmag.com/center-of-attention/|title=Center of Attention - Sacramento King Willie Cauley-Stein|date=October 16, 2017}}</ref> His mother, Marlene Stein, and his father, Willie Cauley, met shortly after high school and never married, and his father left the family shortly after his birth.<ref name="auto"/><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2287213-superstardom-awaits-willie-cauley-steinif-he-finally-decides-he-wants-it|title=Superstardom Awaits Willie Cauley-Stein...If He Finally Decides He Wants It|first=Jason|last=King|website=Bleacher Report}}</ref> His maternal grandparents, Norma and Val Stein, helped raise him, and he legally changed his surname from Cauley to Cauley-Stein.<ref name="auto"/>

==High school career==
As a high school freshman, he was {{convert|6|ft|8|in}}.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://cm.courier-journal.com/offers-reg|title=Special Subscription Offers|website=cm.courier-journal.com}}</ref> As a sophomore he transferred to [[Olathe Northwest High School]] in [[Olathe, Kansas]], where he played basketball and [[American football|football]]. As a junior, he averaged 15.8 points and 8.5 rebounds per game.

Considered a four-star basketball recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Cauley-Stein was listed as the No. 9 center and the No. 40 player in the nation in 2012.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/maple/104709|title=Willie Cauley-Stein|work=Rivals.com|access-date=March 25, 2016}}</ref>

Cauley-Stein was not eligible to play varsity football until his senior year, but he was convinced to play wide receiver when he did. In 2011, he helped his high school win a 7-on-7 football tournament at the [[University of Kansas]] and was offered a football scholarship on the spot. In his senior season, Cauley-Stein averaged 19.7 yards per catch while sometimes playing as cornerback. He finished with 64 catches for 1,265 yards and 15 touchdowns.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportingnews.com/us/ncaa-basketball/news/willie-cauley-stein-football-star-wide-receiver-kentucky-olathe-high-school-nfl/1inde6cyiekw01bwz086uqjaky|title=Cauley-Stein, a monstrous wide receiver|work=sportingnews.com|access-date=November 7, 2018}}</ref>

==College career==
[[File:Willie Cauley-Stein 2015 dunking against Gators.jpg|thumb|left|Cauley-Stein dunks against the Florida Gators his junior season.]]

===Freshman season===
Cauley-Stein started out his college career as a bench center, backing up top prospect [[Nerlens Noel]]. During his time as a back-up, Cauley-Stein ended up averaging 7.8 points on 63.9% field goal shooting, 5.5 rebounds, 1.7 blocks, 1.0 assists, and 0.8 steals in 20 games of play.

Cauley-Stein earned SEC Freshman of the Week honors twice. Cauley-Stein's season high came against [[2012–13 Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball team|Vanderbilt]] as he posted 20 points to go with seven rebounds. A couple of weeks prior, he was a perfect 5-of-5 from the field against [[2012–13 Auburn Tigers men's basketball team|Auburn]].

On February 12, 2013, in a game against [[2012–13 Florida Gators men's basketball team|Florida]], Noel tore the [[Anterior cruciate ligament|ACL]] in his left knee after blocking a lay-up, forcing him to sit out the remainder of the season. Cauley-Stein was given the starting center position due to Noel's season-ending injury. In Noel's absence, he recorded three double-doubles in six games including 10 points and 11 rebounds against [[2012–13 Georgia Bulldogs basketball team|Georgia]] in addition to 13 points, 10 rebounds, and four blocks at [[2012–13 Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball team|Arkansas]]

After SEC play ended he was named to the All-SEC Freshman team. At the end of the season he averaged 8.3 points and 6.2 rebounds per game after appearing in 29 games while making 14 starts.

===Sophomore season===
During the 2013–14 season, he appeared in 37 games, making 18 starts while averaging 6.8 points, 6.1 rebounds, and 2.9 blocks per game. His tallied 106 blocks for the season is a total that ranks as the second most in a single season in school history.

His terrific sophomore season led to him being named to the All-SEC Defensive Team. He recorded a career-high nine blocks twice during the season against [[2013–14 Providence Friars men's basketball team|Providence]] and [[2013–14 Boise State Broncos men's basketball team|Boise State]]. He really started coming into his own towards the end of the season. In the SEC tournament, he recorded 10 points, 11 rebounds, and five blocks versus #1 [[2013–14 Florida Gators men's basketball team|Florida]] in the SEC championship game.

Due to an injury to his leg suffered during the [[2014 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2014 NCAA tournament]] in a game against [[2013–14 Louisville Cardinals men's basketball team|Louisville]], Cauley-Stein missed the remainder of the season. He decided to return for his junior season due to his injury; he was a projected top-15 pick in the [[2014 NBA draft]] prior to his injury.

===Junior season===
In 2014–15, Cauley-Stein was named the SEC Defensive Player of the Year. He was also selected to the All-SEC First Team, the All-SEC Defensive Team and the USA Today first-team All-American Team.

On April 9, 2015, Cauley-Stein, and teammates [[Andrew Harrison (basketball)|Andrew Harrison]], [[Aaron Harrison]], [[Dakari Johnson]], [[Devin Booker]], [[Trey Lyles]], and [[Karl-Anthony Towns]], all declared to enter their names into the [[NBA draft]].

==Professional career==
===Sacramento Kings (2015–2019)===
On June 25, 2015, Cauley-Stein was selected by the [[Sacramento Kings]] with the sixth overall pick in the [[2015 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/kings/kings-select-willie-cauley-stein-first-round|title=Kings Select Willie Cauley-Stein in the First Round|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=June 25, 2015|access-date=June 27, 2015}}</ref> On July 16, he signed with the Kings.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-sign-willie-cauley-stein|title=Kings Sign Willie Cauley-Stein|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=July 16, 2015|access-date=July 17, 2015}}</ref> He made his debut for the Kings in their season opener on October 28, recording two points and two rebounds in a 111–104 loss to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151028/LACSAC/gameinfo.html|title=Griffin leads Clippers past Kings 111–104 in opener|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=October 28, 2015|access-date=October 28, 2015}}</ref> He made his first career start two days later and recorded 17 points and nine rebounds in a 132–114 win over the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref name=br>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/c/caulewi01/gamelog/2016/|title=Willie Cauley-Stein 2015–16 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=December 4, 2015}}</ref> Cauley-Stein missed most of December with a right index finger injury.<ref>{{cite web |last=Singh |first=A. |date=December 3, 2015 |title=Willie Cauley-Stein Injury Update |url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/willie-cauley-stein-injury-update |access-date=October 24, 2023 |publisher=National Basketball Association}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160102/PHXSAC/gameinfo.html|title=Kings beat Suns; coach Karl ties for 5th most wins|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=January 2, 2016|access-date=January 2, 2016}}</ref> On January 20, he recorded his first career double-double with 12 points and 10 rebounds in a 112–93 win over the Lakers.<ref name="br"/> On March 25, he scored a then career-high 26 points in a 116–94 win over the [[Phoenix Suns]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160325/PHXSAC/gameinfo.html|title=Cauley-Stein busts out offensively, Kings beat Suns 116, 94|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=March 25, 2016|access-date=March 25, 2016}}</ref> At the season's end, he earned [[NBA All-Rookie Second Team]] honors.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2016/news/05/19/2015-16-all-rookie-first-and-second-teams-karl-anthony-towns-kristaps-porzingis-devin-booker-nikola-jokic-jahlil-okafor/|title=Wolves' Towns, Knicks' Porzingis lead 2015–16 NBA All-Rookie teams|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=May 19, 2016|access-date=May 19, 2016}}</ref>

On February 23, 2017, following the [[DeMarcus Cousins]] trade, Cauley-Stein was given extended minutes off the bench and came through with a career-high 29 points and 10 rebounds to help the Kings defeat the [[Denver Nuggets]] 116–100.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900261|title=Cauley-Stein scores 29, Kings beat Nuggets 116–100|publisher=ESPN|date=February 23, 2017|access-date=February 24, 2017}}</ref>

On January 6, 2018, Cauley-Stein recorded a career-best seven steals in a 106–98 win over the [[Denver Nuggets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975331|title=Carter has big fourth quarter to lead Kings past Nuggets|publisher=ESPN|date=January 6, 2018|access-date=January 7, 2018}}</ref>

On October 29, 2018, Cauley-Stein scored 26 points and grabbed 13 rebounds in a 123–113 win over the [[Miami Heat]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070770|title=Kings run away after halftime, top Heat 123–113|publisher=ESPN|date=October 29, 2018|access-date=October 29, 2018}}</ref> On December 23, 2018, he had 22 points and a career-high 17 rebounds in a 122–117 win over the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071173|title=Kings rally in 4th quarter to beat Pelicans 122–117|publisher=ESPN|date=December 23, 2018|access-date=December 24, 2018}}</ref>

On June 28, 2019, the Kings extended a qualifying offer to Cauley-Stein in order to make him a [[restricted free agent]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Anderson|first=Jason|url=https://www.sacbee.com/sports/nba/sacramento-kings/article232101497.html|title=Report: Kings give qualifying offer to Willie Cauley-Stein after he asked them not to|work=sacbee.com|date=June 28, 2019|access-date=June 29, 2019}}</ref> The qualifying offer was later rescinded to make more cap space for the Kings to land [[Cory Joseph]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Schmidt|first=Matthew|title=Kings rescind qualifying offer to Willie Cauley-Stein|url=https://clutchpoints.com/kings-news-sacramento-rescind-qualifying-offer-to-willie-cauley-stein/|website=ClutchPoints|access-date=July 9, 2019|date=July 1, 2019}}</ref>

===Golden State Warriors (2019–2020)===
On July 8, 2019, Cauley-Stein signed with the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Warriors Sign Free Agent Center Willie Cauley-Stein|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/cauley-stein-signing-20190708|publisher=National Basketball Association|access-date=July 9, 2019|date=July 8, 2019}}</ref> Cauley-Stein made his Warriors debut on October 10 against the Phoenix Suns, scoring 12 points on 5-of-5 shooting and 2-of-2 from the line, along with five rebounds, one assist, one block, and three fouls in 12 minutes.

===Dallas Mavericks (2020–2022)===
On January 25, 2020, Cauley-Stein was traded to the [[Dallas Mavericks]] for a 2020 second-round pick.<ref>{{cite web |title=Mavericks Acquire Willie Cauley-Stein |url=https://www.mavs.com/mavericks-acquire-willie-cauley-stein/ |publisher=National Basketball Association |access-date=January 26, 2020 |date=January 25, 2020 |archive-date=January 26, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200126183849/https://www.mavs.com/mavericks-acquire-willie-cauley-stein/ |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |date=January 26, 2020 |title=Mavericks acquire Willie Cauley-Stein from Warriors |publisher=National Basketball Association |url=https://www.nba.com/article/2020/01/24/willie-cauley-stein-trade-warriors-mavs |access-date=October 24, 2023}}</ref> He made his debut three days later in a 104–133 loss to the [[Phoenix Suns]], recording four points and two rebounds in 12 minutes.<ref>{{cite news |title=Booker, Ayton lead Suns to 133–104 blowout of Mavericks|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401161348|access-date=January 28, 2020|publisher=ESPN|date=January 28, 2020}}</ref> Cauley-Stein opted out of the resumed season in the [[2020 NBA Bubble]], as he and his partner were expecting a newborn child in July.<ref>{{cite tweet |last=Charania |first=Shams |author-link=Shams Charania |user=ShamsCharania |number=1276205601509474304 |date=June 25, 2020 |title=Mavericks center Willie Cauley-Stein has decided to sit out the resumed NBA season, sources tell @TheAthleticNBA @Stadium. Cauley-Stein and his partner are expecting a newborn child in July. |language=en |access-date=February 28, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210526124722/https://twitter.com/shamscharania/status/1276205601509474304 |archive-date=May 26, 2021 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-12-09 |title=Why Mavs' Willie Cauley-Stein feels his no-bubble offseason prepped him to fill in for Kristaps Porzingis |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/sports/mavericks/2020/12/09/mavs-willie-cauley-stein-feels-his-no-bubble-offseason-prepped-him-to-fill-in-for-kristaps-porzingis/ |access-date=2022-10-10 |website=Dallas News |language=en}}</ref>

After the conclusion of the 2019–20 season, Cauley-Stein declined his option on November 19, 2020, and opted out of his contract, to become a free agent.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sefko |first=Eddie |date=November 19, 2020 |title=Hardaway opts in for coming season |url=https://www.mavs.com/roster-news |access-date=November 19, 2020 |website=mavs.com}}</ref> He later re-signed with the Mavericks on December 1, 2020.<ref>{{cite web |last=Sefko |first=Eddie |date=December 1, 2020 |title=Mavericks sign eight, including Barea, Iwundu, Burke |url=https://www.mavs.com/mavericks-sign-six-including-barea-iwundu-burke/ |access-date=December 1, 2020 |work=mavs.com}}</ref>

The Mavericks picked up his team option on August 1, 2021, keeping Cauley-Stein for the 2021–22 season.<ref>{{cite web |last=Price |first=Dwain |date=August 1, 2021 |title=Mavs pick up team option on Cauley-Stein's contract |url=https://www.mavs.com/cauleysteinreturns |access-date=August 1, 2021 |work=mavs.com}}</ref> On January 15, 2022, the Mavericks decided to waive him in order to make roster room for new signing [[Marquese Chriss]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Mavericks waive Willie Cauley-Stein, sign Marquese Chriss|url=https://www.mavsmoneyball.com/2022/1/15/22885639/mavericks-waive-willie-cauley-stein-sign-marquese-chriss|website=Mavs Moneyball|access-date=January 15, 2022|date=January 15, 2022}}</ref>

===Philadelphia 76ers (2022)===
On February 24, 2022, Cauley-Stein signed a 10-day contract with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Gies |first=Kurt |date=February 24, 2022 |title=76ers Sign Willie Cauley-Stein to 10-Day Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/76ers-sign-willie-cauley-stein |access-date=February 24, 2022 |work=NBA.com}}</ref> He was waived on March 3.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rappaport |first=Max |date=March 3, 2022 |title=76ers Sign DeAndre Jordan |url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/76ers-sign-deandre-jordan |access-date=March 3, 2022 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

===Rio Grande Valley Vipers (2022–2023)===
On October 9, 2022, Cauley-Stein signed with the [[Houston Rockets]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Stein |first=Marc |date=October 10, 2022 |title=The Rockets today made official the long-expected signing of Willie Cauley-Stein. |url=https://twitter.com/thesteinline/status/1579127311592722432 |access-date=2022-10-09 |website=Twitter |language=en}}</ref> On November 3, he was named to the opening night roster for the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/vipers-finalize-2022-23-opening-night-roster/n-5895553|website=oursportscentral.com|title=Vipers Finalize 2022-23 Opening Night Roster|date=November 3, 2022|access-date=November 3, 2022}}</ref> On February 27, 2023, Cauley-Stein signed a 10-day contract with the [[Houston Rockets]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=Joshi |first=Hiren |date=February 27, 2023 |title=Rockets Sign Willie Cauley-Stein to 10-Day Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-sign-willie-cauley-stein-to-10-day-contract |access-date=February 28, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> but he never appeared in a game for the team. After his contract with the Rockets expired, he rejoined the Vipers. On April 9, 2023, Cauley-Stein re-signed with the Rockets.<ref>{{cite tweet|number=1645086120986779648|title=The Rockets today announced they have signed free agent center Willie Cauley-Stein.|user=HoustonRockets|author=Houston Rockets|date=April 9, 2023|access-date=April 9, 2023}}</ref>

===Pallacanestro Varese (2023–2024)===
On July 31, 2023, Cauley-Stein signed with [[Pallacanestro Varese|Openjobmetis Varese]] of the [[Lega Basket Serie A]] (LBA) and [[FIBA Europe Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|title=WILLIE CAULEY-STEIN È IL NUOVO CENTRO DELLA PALLACANESTRO VARESE|url=https://www.pallacanestrovarese.it/news/willie-cauley-stein-e-il-nuovo-centro-della-pallacanestro-varese|website=PallacanestroVarese.it|date=July 31, 2023|access-date=July 31, 2023|language=it}}</ref> He later explained he signed in Europe “because of the more tactical way of playing”.<ref>{{cite web|first=Kurt|last=Helin|title=Willie Cauley-Stein: 'I chose to come to Europe because of the more tactical way of playing'|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nba/news/willie-cauley-stein-i-chose-to-come-to-europe-because-of-the-more-tactical-way-of-playing|website=NBCSports.com|date=September 18, 2023|access-date=October 30, 2023}}</ref> On October 25, Cauley-Stein had 19 points and 20 rebounds in a 91–71 win over [[BG Göttingen]], which set a new FIBA Europe Cup record for most rebounds in a game by a single player.<ref>{{cite web|title=Cauley-Stein breaks FIBA Europe Cup single-game rebounding record|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/europecup/23-24/news/cauley-stein-breaks-fiba-europe-cup-single-game-rebounding-record|website=FIBA.basketball|date=October 26, 2023|access-date=October 30, 2023}}</ref>

On January 30, 2024, Cauley-Stein signed with [[Indios de Mayagüez (basketball)|Indios de Mayagüez]],<ref>{{cite web|first=Luke|last=Adams|title=And-Ones: Cauley-Stein, Rondo, Curry/Ionescu, Silver, Morant|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/01/and-ones-cauley-stein-rondo-curry-ionescu-silver-morant.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=January 30, 2024|access-date=March 18, 2024}}</ref> but left the team on March 24.<ref>{{cite tweet|author=La Guerra del BSN|title=#BSNPR INDIOS CONFIRMAN SALIDA DE CAULEY-STEIN. El ex-NBA Willie Cauley Stein no debutará en el Baloncesto Superior Nacional tras los Indios de Mayagüez dejar en libertad al jugador según confirmó el apoderado Cady Acosta. “No llegó en las condiciones físicas esperadas y tomamos la decisión antes que comenzara la temporada” expresó Acosta. La franquicia se encuentra en busca de otro refuerzo para comenzar la temporada 2024. 📝 Jarniel Canales El Nuevo Día|number=1772018770883568086|user=LaGuerraBSN|date=March 24, 2024|access-date=March 29, 2024|language=Spanish}}</ref>

===Nanjing Monkey Kings (2024)===
On October 21, 2024, Cauley-Stein signed with [[Nanjing Monkey Kings]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] (CBA).<ref>{{cite web |title=冲击季后赛不容有失，同曦官宣签下新外援 |url=https://www.yangtse.com/zncontent/4090837.html |publisher=扬子晚报/紫牛新闻 |access-date=21 October 2024 |date=21 October 2024}}</ref>

==Personal life==
On May 1, 2015, Cauley-Stein officially filed a name-change order with the Probate Division of the Fayette District Court to change his birth name. He did it to honor his mother, Marlene Stein, and his maternal grandparents Norma and Val Stein, who raised him after his father left him when he was four.<ref>{{cite web|last=Johnson|first=Hillary Louise|url=http://www.sactownmag.com/October-November-2017/center-of-Attention/|title=Center of Attention|work=sactownmag.com|date=October 12, 2017|access-date=February 13, 2019}}</ref> He also added "Trill" as a middle name, a nickname given to him by friends.<ref>{{cite web|last=Sherman|first=Rodger|url=https://www.sbnation.com/2015/5/4/8548185/willie-cauley-stein-TRILL-name-nba-draft-kentucky|title=Willie Cauley-Stein legally changes name to 'Willie Trill Cauley-Stein'|work=SBNation.com|date=May 4, 2015|access-date=March 25, 2016}}</ref>

Cauley-Stein's father, Willie Cauley, played college basketball at [[Dodge City Community College]] and for one season at the [[Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball|University of Pittsburgh]]. Willie Cauley met Cauley-Stein's mother, Marlene Stein, while she was playing college basketball for [[St. Mary of the Plains College]].<ref name=Kansas>[https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/ncaa/article17143706.html Willie Cauley-Stein’s path to Final Four with Kentucky started in small Kansas town] Kerkhoff, Blair. ''The Kansas City Star''. www.kansascity.com . Published April 2, 2015. Retrieved June 16, 2020.</ref>

Cauley-Stein has one child, born in 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Willie Trill Cauley-Stein (@pr00fessortrill) posted on Instagram: "Kendrixx Marie Cauley-Stein 07-07-2020 4:44pm 8lbs 15oz 22in Words can't describe how courageous and strong @kels_brooks was during…" • Jul 11, 2020 at 3:40pm UTC|url=https://www.instagram.com/p/CCgdY1Hhuav/ |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/iarchive/s/instagram/CCgdY1Hhuav |archive-date=December 24, 2021 |url-access=limited|access-date=August 10, 2020|website=Instagram|language=en}}{{cbignore}}</ref>{{Primary source inline|date=November 2020}}

In August 2024, Cauley-Stein disclosed that a serious drug addiction was the reason behind his NBA “personal leave” in 2021 and exit in 2022. In an interview with The Athletic's Kyle Tucker, he hopes to make an NBA return and stay clean for his wife and children.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-09-01 |title=Ex-Warriors, Kings player Cauley-Stein reflects on past drug addiction |url=https://www.nbcsportsbayarea.com/nba/golden-state-warriors/willie-cauley-stein-drug-addiction-recovery/1776303/ |access-date=2024-09-02 |website=NBC Sports Bay Area & California |language=en-US}}</ref>
